At a cap of 0.02 the best reaches B_TP = 0.5437 with B dominant-composition 0.6875 -- already above the frozen 0.50 B bar, at one fifth of the A budget.
WHAT_THE_TWO_FEATURE_CONTRAST_ACTUALLY_D.reading: The second feature changed the trade-off qualitatively, not incrementally. The question the PI posed -- 'can the second feature reshape the trade-off enough that the selector fires meaningfully on Pole B while keeping A false positives inside the frozen budget' -- is answered YES on calibration and was not answered on held-out, because the frozen selection rule did not pick a point in that region.
WHAT_THE_TWO_FEATURE_CONTRAST_ACTUALLY_D.caveat_load_bearing: Every frontier number above is CALIBRATION-side. None of it is held-out-verified. The one configuration that was scored held-out is the one the frozen rule selected, and it failed.

WHY_THE_SELECTED_POINT_FAILED.mechanism: The frozen selection rule is 'retain configs with A_FP <= 0.10, then MAXIMIZE B_TP among survivors'. Maximizing the objective against an inequality constraint drives the choice onto the constraint boundary by construction.
WHY_THE_SELECTED_POINT_FAILED.evidence: The selected configuration (W=120, hysteresis=0.0, dwell=4, threshold=-0.7166666666666667) had a calibration A_FP of 0.09635416666666667 -- 96.4% of the entire budget, a margin of 0.0036. The held-out A_FP came in at 0.11197916666666667.
WHY_THE_SELECTED_POINT_FAILED.diagnosis: This is a selection-procedure defect, not a feature defect and not an architecture falsification. A rule with no safety margin against a noisy constraint estimate fails the constraint out of sample roughly half the time. The two-feature statistic was never the thing that broke.
WHY_THE_SELECTED_POINT_FAILED.the_same_rule_did_not_expose_this_on_the: There the constraint region was empty of firing configurations, so the boundary-hugging property had nothing to hug and never showed itself.

THE_OPEN_DECISION_FOR_THE_PI.statement: The PI's branch rule was: safe nonzero region appears -> freeze the operating point and confirm; no safe region appears -> stop hand-tuned selector work because threshold+dwell is the wrong architecture. This run landed between those branches and neither is a clean fit.
THE_OPEN_DECISION_FOR_THE_PI.the_tension: A safe nonzero region DID appear (branch 1's trigger), but the operating point the frozen rule produced from it FAILED held-out confirmation (branch 1's exit condition), for a reason that has nothing to do with the feature or the architecture (branch 2's premise is therefore unsupported).
THE_OPEN_DECISION_FOR_THE_PI.option_A_honour_the_terminal_clause: Treat the frozen FAIL as terminal and stop hand-tuned selector work. Cost: closes a branch on a procedural defect while the evidence says the mechanism works, and discards a statistic (P_red) that separates the poles perfectly.
THE_OPEN_DECISION_FOR_THE_PI.option_B_one_margin_aware_reselection: A fresh freeze whose selection rule targets a MARGIN against the A_FP cap instead of maximizing B_TP at the boundary -- for example, select the max-B_TP configuration subject to A_FP <= 0.05, or specify the constraint at the episode level with a one-sided bound. Fresh held-out block 99900501-516. This is a fix to the selection rule, not a new knob on the selector, and it is one shot.
THE_OPEN_DECISION_FOR_THE_PI.why_this_is_a_PI_call_and_not_an_agent_c: The PI's standing direction was to stop tuning knobs. Option B is defensible as repairing a procedural defect rather than tuning, but that judgement belongs to the PI. No agent should make it by inference, and nothing in this reading may be read as having made it.
THE_OPEN_DECISION_FOR_THE_PI.what_the_agent_did_not_do: No configuration was re-selected, no held-out block was re-scored, no gate was relaxed, and no further episode was collected after the frozen pass completed.

claim_boundary: Calibration only. No outcome episode was run in this branch. Nothing here establishes any win-rate result, and the composition effect itself remains established only under oracle regime labels.
